1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. The exam at a glance. The five domains. How adaptive testing works. What the twenty twenty-six outline changed. How to answer every question. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Exam overview, domain map and answer technique (all domains). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. Exam. I S C two C C, the entry-level cybersecurity exam from I S C two. Format. Computerized Adaptive Testing (C A T). Items. one hundred to one hundred twenty-five; multiple choice and advanced item types. Time. two hours at most. Passing grade. seven hundred out of one thousand points. Languages. English, Chinese, Japanese, German, Spanish. Testing. At a Pearson testing center. Prerequisites. None; basic I T knowledge is recommended and no work experience is required. The price, the validity of the credential and the yearly maintenance terms are not in the outline, so this course does not quote them. Check the official I S C two pages before you book. Exam tip: The exam is for beginners, but it is wide. It asks for definitions and the best action, not for commands. Learn the vocabulary exactly.

1.title: The five domains
1.text: The five domains. The figure shows this: Domain map: five domains, their weights and the modules that cover them.

1.title: The five domains, continued
1.text: The five domains. one. Security Principles. Weight: twenty-four percent. Topics: C I A and A A A, risk management, governance, controls, ethics. two. Security Governance. Weight: seventeen point three percent. Topics: G R C, business continuity and disaster recovery, awareness, metrics. three. Identity and Access Management (I A M) Concepts. Weight: twenty percent. Topics: Identity life cycle, logical access controls.

1.title: The five domains, continued
1.text: The five domains. four. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts. Weight: twenty-one point three percent. Topics: Network security, architecture, cloud security. five. Security Operations and Incident Response. Weight: seventeen point three percent. Topics: Data security, operations, incident response, assets, testing. Exam tip: Domain one is the largest (twenty-four percent), then Domain four (twenty-one point three percent) and Domain three (twenty percent). The two smallest are both seventeen point three percent.

1.title: How adaptive testing works
1.text: How adaptive testing works. Item choice. The next item depends on your earlier answers; each item aims for about a fifty percent chance of a correct answer, so expect every item to feel hard. Unscored items. twenty-five of the items are pretest items that do not count; you cannot tell them apart. Minimum for a result. At least seventy-five scored items plus the twenty-five pretest items, one hundred in all. End of the exam. It stops when the system is ninety-five percent confident that you are above or below the passing standard, or at one hundred twenty-five items, or when two hours are over.

1.title: How adaptive testing works, continued
1.text: How adaptive testing works. Review. Item review is not permitted: an answer is final once you give it. Result. Shown right after the exam; a failing candidate gets a level per domain (Below, Near or Above proficiency). Retakes. Wait thirty days after the first attempt, sixty after the second, ninety after the third; at most four attempts in twelve months. Exam tip: You cannot go back. Read each item, decide, and move on. A long exam is not a bad sign: the system may need more items to be sure.

1.title: What the 2026 outline changed
1.text: What the twenty twenty-six outline changed. The outline that took effect on September one, twenty twenty-six replaced the older one. It still has five domains, with new names and weights. Business continuity, disaster recovery and incident response was a domain (ten percent). Security Governance (seventeen point three percent); B C and D R sit under redundancy, and incident response moved into Domain five. Access Controls Concepts. Identity and Access Management Concepts, with the identity life cycle. Network Security. Networking and Cloud Security Concepts, with cloud, zero trust and segmentation. A I security is built into all five domains: protecting training data and model integrity, A I-driven phishing, model drift as a recovery risk, bots and service accounts in the identity life cycle, A I in firewalls and sim tools, and the security of the A I workspace.

1.title: How to answer every question
1.text: How to answer every question. Read the last line to see what is asked: a definition, a best action, a control type or a first step. Find the domain: principles, governance, access, network and cloud, or operations. Eliminate answers that are too technical, too late in the process, or that break a principle such as least privilege. When two answers seem right, pick the one that is preventive, simple and within policy. Never leave a blank; you cannot return. Exam tip: The best answer is often the first step, the least privilege or the answer that follows policy and escalates, not the most technical fix.

1.title: A study plan
1.text: A study plan. one. Modules: one to four. Goal: Principles: C I A, risk, governance, controls, ethics. two. Modules: five to six. Goal: Governance: G R C, continuity, awareness, metrics. three. Modules: seven to eight. Goal: Identity and access management. four. Modules: nine to twelve. Goal: Networks, architecture and cloud. five. Modules: thirteen to seventeen. Goal: Data, operations, incident response, assets, testing. six. Modules: eighteen. Goal: Exam technique and final review.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A candidate asks what score is needed to pass the I S C two C C exam. Which statement is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: seven hundred out of one thousand points on the adaptive exam. The passing grade is seven hundred out of one thousand points.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. During the adaptive exam, a candidate wants to go back to question twelve to change an answer. What is the rule? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Item review is not permitted, so an answer is final. The adaptive exam does not allow item review.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A candidate wonders how many scored items are needed for a pass or fail result. What is the minimum? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: At least seventy-five scored items plus the twenty-five pretest items. A result needs at least seventy-five scored items and the twenty-five unscored pretest items, one hundred in all.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which domain carries the largest weight in the current outline? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Security Principles, with twenty-four percent of the exam. Security Principles is the largest domain at twenty-four percent.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Compared with the older outline, where did incident response move in the twenty twenty-six outline? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Into Domain five, Security Operations and Incident Response. Incident response became a major part of Domain five, and the standalone domain was replaced by Security Governance.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A candidate fails the first attempt. How long must the candidate wait before the second attempt? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: thirty days after the first attempt. The wait is thirty days after the first attempt, sixty after the second and ninety after the third.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the exam? Answer: Up to two hours. Question two. How many items does the exam have? Answer: one hundred to one hundred twenty-five. Question three. How many of the items are unscored? Answer: twenty-five pretest items.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the weight of Domain four? Answer: twenty-one point three percent. Question five. Can you review a previous answer? Answer: No, item review is not permitted. Question six. How many attempts are allowed in twelve months? Answer: At most four.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: adaptive, one hundred to one hundred twenty-five items, two hours, seven hundred of one thousand. Weights: twenty-four or seventeen point three or twenty or twenty-one point three or seventeen point three percent. Adaptive rules: twenty-five unscored, at least seventy-five scored, ninety-five percent confidence, no review. Retakes: thirty, sixty, ninety days; four attempts in twelve months. twenty twenty-six changes: Security Governance added; I A M; cloud and zero trust; A I integrated. Method: find the domain, eliminate, pick the preventive, policy-based answer.
